props.gloss_en: one may not send a letter in the hand of a gentile on Shabbat eve unless he fixes a fee for him
the baraita's seifa, following its fixed-fee clause: Beit Shammai -- time for him to reach his house; Beit Hillel -- time to reach the house adjacent to the wall
Beit Shammai: [one may send it only with time enough] for him to reach his house
Beit Hillel: [with time enough] for him to reach the house adjacent to the wall
Rav Sheshet: this is what it says -- and if he did NOT fix a fee, Beit Shammai: until he reaches his house; Beit Hillel: until he reaches the house adjacent to the wall
this [the seifa, which lets him send without a fee] is where a post-house is fixed in the town
that [the reisha, which requires a fee] is where no post-house is fixed in the town

objections.gloss_en: והלא קצץ? -- but he has fixed a fee! [read after the fixed-fee clause, the Beit Shammai / Beit Hillel time limits make no sense]

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמר: ואם לא קצץ -- the time limits concern the case where he did NOT fix a fee (= p_rsh_hachi_kaamar)

objections.gloss_en: והאמרת רישא אין משלחין? -- but you said in the first clause one may not send [unless he fixes a fee]!

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא דקביע בי דואר במתא, והא דלא קביע בי דואר במתא -- the seifa is where a post-house is fixed in the town, the reisha where none is (= p_seifa_kvia_bei_doar, p_reisha_lo_kvia_bei_doar)
